questions.stem: T is exponential with mean 4 minutes. Its rate λ is…
questions.incorrectFeedback: For the exponential, the rate is 1 over the mean: 1/4 per minute. A rate of 4 per minute would mean a 15-second average wait.

questions.stem: T is exponential and P(T > 5) = 0.6. What is P(T > 8 | T > 3)?
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — memoryless: given 3 survived, needing 5 more has chance P(T > 5) = 0.6.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Memorylessness: P(T > 3 + 5 | T > 3) = P(T > 5) = 0.6. The 3 units already survived don't count.

questions.stem: Buses arrive Poisson-style at 4 per hour. P(waiting more than 15 minutes) is…
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — 15 minutes expects 4 × 1/4 = 1 bus, and an empty window has chance e^(−1).
questions.incorrectFeedback: Waiting more than 15 minutes means no bus in a quarter hour, where λ = 4 × 1/4 = 1. So the chance is e^(−1) ≈ 0.37.

questions.stem: From Lesson 10: which discrete distribution is memoryless?
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — the geometric; today's exponential is its continuous twin.
questions.incorrectFeedback: The geometric wait is the discrete memoryless one: P(X > m + k | X > m) = P(X > k). The exponential is its continuous twin.
